Comments of the Florida Audubon Society --
Because of Man's increasing population, the loss of natural resources due to widespread development, and increasing pollution among other things, all wildlife is placed in the "endangered" category. Existing laws attempt to protect the most endangered. This is a relative thing. Questions remain: At what point does the population of a species reach a point of no return? How many Southern Bald Eagle nests are required to maintain a healthy population? Are 2,000 Dusky Seaside Sparrows enough to prevent eventual extinction of the species.
The Federal government still does not show enough concern over even the "endangered" species on the list of the U. S. Department of the Interior. Construction of a highway is being allowed that cuts through the habitat of the Dusky Seaside Sparrow in spite of suitable alternates to the present route. Is the construction of a relatively unnecessary highway worth the risk of extinction of a species? Remaining habitats of the Florida manatee are being lost to development at a rapid rate. Habitat of the Everglade Kite has been suddenly drained in order to protect agricultural interests who have been heavily subsidized by the U. S. government.
Pesticides are constantly being sprayed on our environment with improper controls in spite of known disastrous effects on wildlife. Apparently it will take some kind of human disaster to create common sense controls of pesticides. In the meantime, wildlife suffers terribly.
Apparently many State wildlife agencies obtain most of their funding from the sale of hunting and fishing licenses. Because of this, the Florida Game and Fresh Water Fish Commission concentrates its attention on game birds and fish. The populations of non-game wildlife go unattended. Private groups such as the Audubon Society are forced to devote a great deal of time protecting wildlife as best they can.
THE DRAFT IMPACT STATEMENT FAILS TO GO INTO DETAIL REGARDING THE ENFORCEMENT OF THE ENDANGERED SPECIES ACT. HOW MANY CONVICTIONS. HAVE THE THREE ENFORCEMENT OFFICERS IN FLORIDA OBTAINED SINCE THE ACT WAS PASSED? THE DRAFT STATES THAT $15 MILLION WAS SPENT TO ACQUIRE ENDANGERED SPECIES HABITAT. WHERE WAS THIS MONEY SPENT? THERE ALSO SEEMS TO BE CONFUSION REGARDING THE IMPORTATION OF FOREIGN ENDANGERED WILDLIFE. ENFORCEMENT OFFICERS OF THE U.S. DEPARTMENT OF INTERIOR SEEM TO HAVE PROBLEMS REGARDING FOREIGN LAWS WHICH PERTAIN TO ENDANGERED WILDLIFE. PRIME BALD EAGLE HABITAT HAS BEEN FOUND IN FLORIDA AT REASONABLE PRICES, YET WE ARE ASKED TO "PROMOTE INTEREST" REGARDING THE FEDERAL ACQUISITION OF THESE LANDS.
The Florida Audubon Society is opposed to the section of the proposed legislation which allows the Secretary to grant one-year permits to any person who would suffer under economic hardship for the importing exporting, taking or transporting of species or subspecies appearing on the lister. ALLICATOR I ACCEPTED ALL DREM TO BE "HEROSHIP" CASES.
